scope.e2_protocol: Section 3.6 plus Amendment v2.2 A9: 1,000 categorical realizations of every fit row per pattern, PCG64 seeded from the big-endian integer represented by the first 64 SHA-256 bits of qrf-drift-v2.2|C0b|target|pattern|replicate; MC mean tested with the exact fit-row one-draw SD/sqrt(R), plus the frozen recipient production one-realization z; exact rule for p in {0,1}.
scope.e4_method: restore state-before fit RNG; use its first integer as the exact HistGradientBoostingClassifier random_state; direct donor weights; restore state-before draw RNG; consume one magnitude quantile per recipient then consume gate uniforms; compare sign codes to the bank raw-draw sign vector

conclusion.instrument_implication: The frozen control cannot be executed uniquely from the design text and persisted inputs. This is a specification failure, not evidence of a numerical gate defect.
conclusion.phase0_implication: Do not claim a C4 pass or numerical failure from this work. No full /tmp/qrf_phase0_v22_c4.json was produced.
conclusion.summary: A10 uniquely supplies the donor self-substitution exchangeability idea, the v2.2 seed namespace, the zero expectation, and the pass inequality, but it inherits an A8 target-level weighted-stratified recipient subsample whose allocation, within-stratum draw, weighting, and aggregation algorithms are not frozen. These choices change the Monte Carlo standard errors and can change the C4 pass/fail result. Selecting them during the permitted rerun would be a new post-freeze control specification.

deterministic_pattern_GQ_census.reason: No target pattern x GQ census was already available. A seedless reconstruction attempt stopped before any RNG when the exploratory loader encountered null TYPEHUGQ values on all-origin rows; per instruction it was not repaired or rerun. No C4 seed was consumed by that attempt.

incorrect_benchmark_disclosure.interpretation: The three benchmark rows happened to pass under the incorrect protocol. They are neither valid C4 statistics nor evidence that the correctly specified control would pass. The consumed v2.2 C4 seed indices are disclosed so they cannot be silently reused as fresh control draws.
incorrect_benchmark_disclosure.why_incorrect: It used n=min(100000, clone0 recipient rows) independently for one target-pattern. A8's wording and the subsequent execution clarification require one target-level n allocated over pattern x GQ strata.

input_integrity_before_benchmark.verified_files: D0 JSON, operative v2.2 design, candidate assembled and transferred checkpoints, all nine current target bank checkpoints, and the three A12 predecessor bank checkpoints

candidate_choices: proportional to physical clone-0 row count with largest-remainder rounding
proportional to exact artifact-weight mass with largest-remainder rounding
Neyman/variance allocation
equal allocation
any of the above with or without a minimum of one draw for every nonempty stratum
unresolved_bindings.issue: Integer allocation of the target-level n=min(100000, |S_q|) over pattern x GQ strata is absent.
unresolved_bindings.numeric_effect: The allocation sets every target-pattern and GQ cell's number of Monte Carlo rows. It changes replicate variance, MC-SE, the [2,4] escalation trigger, and potentially the final Sidak pass/fail decision. Tiny pattern/GQ strata can receive zero or one row depending on the unstated rounding/minimum convention.
unresolved_bindings.textual_evidence: A8 lines 549-553 names the total sample size, the strata, and unbiasedness, but no n_h allocation formula or rounding rule.

candidate_choices: PPS with replacement and an unweighted stratum sample mean
PPS without replacement with exact first-order inclusion probabilities and Horvitz-Thompson weights
successive weighted sampling without replacement with Hajek normalization
uniform sampling with retained artifact weights
unresolved_bindings.issue: The within-stratum weighted sampling design is absent.
unresolved_bindings.numeric_effect: All can be arranged to target the weighted mean but have different realized samples, finite-population corrections, replicate covariance, and MC-SE. Without-replacement methods also need a uniquely bound inclusion-probability implementation.
unresolved_bindings.textual_evidence: A8 says seeded weighted-stratified subsample and unbiased for the weighted mean, but it does not say with versus without replacement or name an inclusion-probability algorithm.

candidate_choices: binary housing-unit versus any group-quarters
three-way TYPEHUGQ 1 versus 2 versus 3
unresolved_bindings.issue: GQ status levels are not enumerated.
unresolved_bindings.numeric_effect: The choice changes the stratum census, integer allocations, and stratified Monte Carlo variance.
unresolved_bindings.textual_evidence: A8 line 551 says GQ status; section 3.4 separately distinguishes housing units, TYPEHUGQ 2, and TYPEHUGQ 3, but A8 does not say binary H/GQ or three-way H/2/3.

candidate_choices: exact target-level stratum weight shares
exact within-pattern GQ shares followed by exact section-3.1 pattern alpha
realized sample shares
per-pattern normalized outputs without alpha scaling
unresolved_bindings.issue: The aggregation estimator from stratum outputs to pattern and target outputs is absent.
unresolved_bindings.numeric_effect: The first two can be algebraically consistent if fully specified; the other choices generally differ. Scaling a cell by a fixed alpha leaves its z unchanged, but allocation and multi-stratum weighting do not. Cross-stratum covariance also affects target-level MC-SE.
unresolved_bindings.textual_evidence: A8 requires unbiasedness but does not state whether to aggregate using exact stratum artifact-weight shares, realized sample shares, or retained row weights. Section 3.1 defines exact pattern alpha weights but A8 does not connect its stratum estimator to them.

candidate_choices: unit analysis weights because the synthetic rows are already PPS donor draws
retain a separately sampled A8 recipient artifact-weight vector while replacing only its X values
attach sampled donor fit weights, which square-weights the synthetic source unless the substitution design is changed correspondingly
unresolved_bindings.issue: The synthetic recipient analysis-weight convention is absent after A10 replaces recipient rows.
unresolved_bindings.numeric_effect: Unit weights and an independent retained recipient-weight vector both preserve exchangeability but yield different conditional variance. Attaching donor fit weights changes the target distribution and can violate A10's source=target claim.
unresolved_bindings.textual_evidence: Section 3.2 line 214 says retain recipient artifact weights. A10 lines 584-586 replaces recipient rows by fit-weight-proportional donor samples, which have donor fit weights rather than recipient artifact weights, and does not say what analysis weight synthetic rows carry.

candidate_choices: PCG64, big-endian first 8 SHA-256 bytes, base sample then substitution sample
PCG64 with little-endian conversion
another NumPy bit generator/default RNG
two child streams derived from the replicate seed
unresolved_bindings.issue: The C4 RNG engine, first-64-bit byte order, and within-replicate stream partition are absent.
unresolved_bindings.numeric_effect: These choices change every realized donor index and therefore each estimate, MC-SE, escalation decision, and output digest.
unresolved_bindings.textual_evidence: A10 binds a seed text but, unlike A9, does not name PCG64. Neither A10 nor section 3.2 states big- versus little-endian conversion or how the independent base-row and substitution-row draws consume the stream.

candidate_choices: main Shapley only
main Shapley plus the 36 A1 C4 statistics
all reported derived rows including interaction/residual
unresolved_bindings.issue: The phrase any contribution in the adaptive trigger does not enumerate whether A1 per-prior outputs and the reported G3 interaction participate.
unresolved_bindings.numeric_effect: The trigger determines whether seeds 250-999 are consumed and changes final MC-SEs.
unresolved_bindings.textual_evidence: A1 makes 36 per-prior outputs C4 statistics. A8 line 554 says any target-pattern where a contribution is in [2,4], but does not explicitly list main Shapley, A1 marginal outputs, the nonallocated interaction, or the cross-group residual.

what_is_uniquely_bound.binding: Synthetic recipient covariates and coalition-substitution covariates are independent samples from the same fit-weight-proportional donor distribution; source and target therefore coincide in expectation.
All 2^3 G1/G2/G3 coalitions, joint same-row copies within a coalition, and common donor draws across coalitions.
Each G3 prior is substituted alone from the same drawn donor row; it is a marginal output and does not sum to G3 Shapley.
Start at 250 and escalate a target-pattern to 1,000 when a contribution has absolute estimate divided by MC-SE in [2,4].
qrf-drift-v2.2|C4|<target>|<pattern>|<replicate>; pass when absolute contribution is at most 3.673063850314496 times its MC-SE; 20 empty-G3 outputs are exact-zero checks.

bound.value: 100 stochastic main-group C4 statistics, 20 deterministic empty-G3 exact zeros, 36 stochastic G3 per-prior statistics; K=214; z*=3.673063850314496

Per target and pattern, eight coalitions over G1/G2/G3; one fit-weight-proportional donor row per recipient; all coalition columns copied from the same row; recipient artifact weights retained; common donor draws across coalitions; Shapley from coalition probability means.

Each prior is substituted one at a time from the same drawn donor row with every other column retained at recipient values; the marginals do not sum to G3 and their difference is a reported interaction.

Total stated sample size min(100000, |S_q|), pattern-by-GQ stratification, initial 250 replicates, target-pattern escalation to 1000 when a contribution has |value|/MC-SE in [2,4], and replicate spread intended to cover row-subsample plus donor-draw randomness.

Recipients are to be replaced by an independent fit-weight-proportional donor-row sample of the A8 subsample size; C4 seed labels are qrf-drift-v2.2|C4|<target>|<pattern>|<replicate>; stochastic statistics use |mean contribution| <= z* times MC SE; empty G3 is exact zero.

formal_a1_counterexample.claim_under_audit: A10 says that donor self-substitution makes source and target coincide and every stochastic contribution have expectation zero.
formal_a1_counterexample.construction: Let a prior X and a retained predictor Y be perfectly correlated, with X=Y and P(X=1)=P(X=0)=1/2. Let the evaluated gate-probability function be f(X,Y)=X*Y. Draw the substituted donor prior X_prime independently from the identical joint donor population, as A10 requires. A1 retains recipient Y and substitutes X alone.
formal_a1_counterexample.reason: Independent one-column substitution breaks cross-column dependence. Exact full-group Shapley contributions can cancel under source-target exchangeability through coalition/complement symmetry, but A1's one-at-a-time marginals are not that symmetric estimator.

material_gaps.choice: Whether every pattern receives N=min(100000,|S_q|), or N is target-level and allocated into n_pattern,GQ cells; if allocated, the allocation and integer-rounding rule.
material_gaps.evidence: A8 states one sample size and pattern-by-GQ strata, while both section 3.2 and A10 define target-pattern computations and seeds; no cell-size rule is present.
material_gaps.numeric_effect: Changes observations per pattern, Monte Carlo variance, MC SE, escalation, and potentially pass/fail.

material_gaps.choice: PPS versus simple sampling within strata, replacement versus no replacement, fixed versus random stratum allocation, and the corresponding unweighted, Horvitz-Thompson, or Hajek estimator.
material_gaps.evidence: A8 names weighted-stratified subsampling and unbiasedness but no inclusion probabilities, replacement rule, allocation, or estimator.
material_gaps.numeric_effect: Multiple procedures satisfy the prose requirement of an unbiased weighted-mean estimate but produce different finite-sample contributions and MC SEs.

material_gaps.choice: Whether a synthetic donor recipient carries its sampled fit weight, unit weight, an inverse-selection weight, or the independently selected original ACS recipient artifact weight.
material_gaps.evidence: Section 3.2 requires retained recipient artifact weights, while A10 replaces recipient rows with fit-weight-PPS donor rows and does not define their artifact weights.
material_gaps.numeric_effect: Carrying fit weights after PPS creates a squared-weight target distribution and generally destroys the claimed exchangeability; unit weights and independent ACS weights both preserve a zero-centered main Shapley null but yield different values and MC SEs.

material_gaps.choice: Whether GQ controls original ACS weight-vector selection, donor sampling, both, or neither after recipient replacement.
material_gaps.evidence: A8 requires pattern-by-GQ strata, A10 prescribes only fit-weight-proportional donor sampling, and section 3.2 excludes GQ as a feature group.
material_gaps.numeric_effect: Changes pattern-cell composition, retained weights, and replicate variance.

material_gaps.choice: Bit generator, replicate index origin, and deterministic stream splitting or call order between recipient-donor sampling and coalition hot-deck sampling.
material_gaps.evidence: A10 binds seed labels but not the PRNG or stream mapping. A9 explicitly binds PCG64 for C0b, so A9's PRNG clause cannot silently supply A10's missing rule. Section 3.2 binds first-64-bit SHA seed conversion for reading seeds but does not name a generator.
material_gaps.numeric_effect: Changes every finite seeded sample and therefore all contributions and MC SEs.

material_gaps.choice: Whether an A1 per-prior sub-attribution counts as a contribution that triggers target-pattern escalation, and the sample-SD degrees-of-freedom convention used in MC SE.
material_gaps.evidence: A8 says any contribution triggers escalation; A1 calls its 36 outputs sub-attributions/marginal contributions; no explicit inclusion or MC-SE formula is given.
material_gaps.numeric_effect: Can change replicate counts and borderline threshold results.
